question.text: The emf of a cell is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> and internal resistance is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo></math><math><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math>. What will be the reading (in volt) of a voltmeter having an internal resistance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></math> <math><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω?</mi></math>

solution.text:
Total resistance=2.5+0.5=3.0 kΩ=3000 Ω

∴ Current, i=63000 A;

Reading of voltmeter =i×2.5×1000

=63000×2500=5 V
